# E-Commerce Shopping Mall Platform Implementation Requirements

## Authentication & Account Management Implementation

### Customer Account
- Implement customer registration with email/password validation
- Implement customer login with JWT token generation
- Implement customer password change with current password verification
- Implement customer account deletion with cascade handling (preserve orders, mark reviews as deleted user)
- Implement customer profile view and edit (display name, phone number) with snapshot creation

### Seller Account
- Implement seller registration with email/password validation
- Implement seller login with JWT token generation
- Implement seller password change with current password verification
- Implement seller account deletion with validation (no pending orders, no pending cancellation/refund requests)
- Implement seller approval status view (pending, approved, rejected with reason)
- Implement seller re-registration after rejection
- Implement seller account deletion cascade (delete products, preserve order history, preserve shop name in past orders)

### Administrator Account
- Implement administrator request submission with reason
- Implement administrator approval/rejection (super admin only)
- Implement administrator grade promotion/demotion (super admin only, cannot demote self)

## Address Management Implementation
- Implement list customer addresses
- Implement create new shipping address with validation
- Implement update shipping address
- Implement delete shipping address
- Implement set default shipping address

## Category Management Implementation
- Implement list all categories (with subcategories)
- Implement view category details with products
- Implement create category (admin only)
- Implement update category (admin only)
- Implement delete category (admin only, products become uncategorized)

## Product Management Implementation
- Implement product creation (seller only) with required fields validation
- Implement product update (seller only) with snapshot creation
- Implement product deletion (seller/admin only) with validation (no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund)
- Implement product detail view with all fields
- Implement product listing with search, filter (category, price range, in-stock), sort (newest, price), pagination
- Implement product snapshot viewing (seller and admin access)
- Implement product image upload, reorder, and deletion
- Implement product visibility after deletion (hidden from search/categories)
- Implement product visibility when seller is suspended (hidden from search/categories)

## Product Variant (SKU) Management Implementation
- Implement add variant to product (seller only) with required fields validation
- Implement update variant (seller only) with snapshot creation
- Implement delete variant (seller only) with validation (no pending order items, no pending cancellation/refund)
- Implement variant SKU uniqueness validation
- Implement variant price override (optional, defaults to base price if not provided)
- Implement variant stock quantity validation (required, starts at 0)
- Implement product with no variants (visible but unavailable)
- Implement variant snapshot viewing

## Inventory Management Implementation
- Implement view inventory history for variant (all records)
- Implement add inventory (restock) with quantity and reason
- Implement subtract inventory (adjustment/loss) with quantity and reason
- Implement automatic inventory decrease on order placement (negative record)
- Implement automatic inventory increase on order cancellation (positive record)
- Implement automatic inventory increase on refund (positive record)
- Implement out of stock variant visibility (stock = 0)
- Implement out of stock variant blocking from cart

## Wishlist Management Implementation
- Implement add product to wishlist
- Implement remove product from wishlist
- Implement view customer wishlist with pagination
- Implement automatic wishlist cleanup when product is deleted (cascade)
- Implement wishlist shows products not variants

## Shopping Cart Implementation
- Implement add variant to cart with quantity
- Implement combine quantities for same variant in cart (update, not create new)
- Implement update cart item quantity
- Implement remove item from cart
- Implement view cart with all details (product name, variant options, price, quantity, subtotal)
- Implement stock validation in cart (warning when stock < quantity)
- Implement marking unavailable variants in cart (deleted or out of stock)
- Implement cart total calculation
- Implement checkout blocking for unavailable items

## Checkout & Order Management Implementation
- Implement order summary review before checkout (items, prices, shipping address, total)
- Implement order placement with payment processing (assume external gateway)
- Implement order placement with payment success (create order, decrease stock, remove cart items)
- Implement order placement with payment failure (no order created, allow retry)
- Implement order item creation with status "paid"
- Implement order item snapshot creation (product, variant, seller profile at time of purchase)
- Implement order history view with pagination (newest first)
- Implement order detail view with all fields (items, shipping address, shipments)
- Implement order status calculation based on item statuses (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded, partially completed)
- Implement mixed order states handling

## Shipping & Tracking Implementation
- Implement view order items needing shipping (seller only, status = paid)
- Implement create shipment with tracking information (carrier name, tracking number)
- Implement bundling multiple items into one shipment (same seller)
- Implement separate shipments for different sellers
- Implement item status change to "shipped" on shipment creation
- Implement view shipment tracking (customer)
- Implement delivery confirmation per shipment (customer only)
- Implement item status change to "delivered" on confirmation
- Implement automatic delivery after 14 days from shipping (scheduled job)

## Order Cancellation Implementation
- Implement request cancellation for paid order item (customer only, status = paid)
- Implement cancellation request with reason
- Implement seller approval of cancellation request
- Implement seller rejection of cancellation request
- Implement cancellation request snapshot creation on status change
- Implement stock restoration on cancellation (positive inventory record)
- Implement order status update when all items cancelled
- Implement cancellation blocking for shipped items (status != paid)
- Implement admin force-cancel functionality (refund customer, restore stock)

## Refund Request Implementation
- Implement request refund for delivered order item (customer only, status = delivered)
- Implement refund request with reason
- Implement 7-day refund window validation (from delivery date)
- Implement seller approval of refund request
- Implement seller rejection of refund request
- Implement refund request snapshot creation on status change
- Implement stock restoration on refund (positive inventory record)
- Implement order status update when all items refunded
- Implement refund blocking for non-delivered items (status != delivered)
- Implement admin force-refund functionality

## Reviews & Ratings Implementation
- Implement create review for delivered order item (customer only)
- Implement review with rating (1-5 stars, required)
- Implement review with optional text content
- Implement one review per product per order validation
- Implement review blocking for non-delivered items
- Implement review update with snapshot creation
- Implement review deletion with snapshot preservation
- Implement view product reviews sorted by newest
- Implement product average rating calculation
- Implement average rating excludes deleted reviews

## Seller Dashboard Implementation
- Implement view shop summary (product count, order item count, pending cancellation count, pending refund count)
- Implement view order items for seller's products
- Implement filter order items by status
- Implement seller access control (only own products/orders)

## Administrator Oversight Implementation
- Implement view all products (admin only)
- Implement view all orders (admin only)
- Implement view all customers (admin only)
- Implement view all sellers (admin only)
- Implement view pending seller approvals
- Implement approve seller registration
- Implement reject seller registration with reason
- Implement suspend seller account (hide products, block new purchases, allow existing order processing, block new product creation/edit)
- Implement unsuspend seller account (products become visible)
- Implement ban customer (cannot login)
- Implement unban customer
- Implement ban seller (cannot login, existing orders remain)
- Implement view product snapshots (admin)
- Implement view order item snapshots (admin)
- Implement view cancellation/refund request snapshots (admin)
- Implement view review snapshots (admin)
- Implement view seller profile snapshots (admin)

## Snapshot System Implementation
- Implement product snapshot creation on edit (all fields, variant snapshots)
- Implement variant snapshot creation on edit
- Implement seller profile snapshot creation on edit
- Implement review snapshot creation on edit
- Implement cancellation request snapshot creation on status change
- Implement refund request snapshot creation on status change
- Implement snapshots are immutable (no update/delete)
- Implement snapshot viewing by relevant parties (owners, admins)
- Implement snapshots preserved after entity deletion

## Multi-Seller Order Implementation
- Implement order with items from multiple sellers
- Implement separate shipments for different sellers
- Implement order item grouping by seller
- Implement independent cancellation/refund per seller's items
- Implement order status with mixed seller items

## Security & Access Control Implementation
- Implement JWT authentication for all protected endpoints
- Implement role-based access control (customer, seller, admin, super admin)
- Implement resource ownership validation (users can only access their own resources)
- Implement admin-only endpoint protection
- Implement seller-only endpoint protection
- Implement customer-only endpoint protection

## Validation & Error Handling Implementation
- Implement input validation for all endpoints
- Implement proper error messages for validation failures
- Implement business rule validation (e.g., cancellation only for paid items)
- Implement proper HTTP status codes
- Implement transaction management for multi-step operations
- Implement rollback on failure

## Data Integrity Implementation
- Implement order history preserved after customer deletion
- Implement reviews preserved as "deleted user" after customer deletion
- Implement order history preserved after seller deletion
- Implement shop name preserved in past orders after seller deletion
- Implement products deleted from listings after seller deletion
- Implement snapshots preserved after product deletion

import { TypedBody, TypedParam, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IEcommerceCustomer } from "../../../api/structures/IEcommerceCustomer";
import { IPageIEcommerceCustomer } from "../../../api/structures/IPageIEcommerceCustomer";
import { getEcommerceCustomersCustomerId } from "../../../providers/getEcommerceCustomersCustomerId";
import { patchEcommerceCustomers } from "../../../providers/patchEcommerceCustomers";

@Controller("/ecommerce/customers")
export class EcommerceCustomersController {
  /**
   * Retrieve a paginated list of customer accounts with optional search filters and sorting.
   *
   * This endpoint supports administrative browsing of customer accounts with filtering by display name, email, registration date range, and account status. Results are returned in paginated format with cursor-based navigation for efficient large dataset handling.
   *
   * **Search Capabilities**
   *
   * - Filter by display name (partial match)
   * - Filter by email (partial match)
   * - Filter by registration date range (created_at)
   * - Filter by account status (active, deleted)
   * - Sort by any field with ascending or descending order
   * - Pagination with limit and offset parameters
   *
   * **Access Control**
   *
   * - Administrators can browse all customer accounts
   * - Customers cannot access this endpoint (data isolation policy)
   *
   * **Data Privacy**
   *
   * - Password hashes are never exposed
   * - Soft-deleted customers are included when filtering by status
   * - Deleted customers show minimal information for privacy compliance
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria for filtering customer accounts including display name, email, registration date range, account status, sorting preferences, and pagination parameters.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor null
   * @x-autobe-specification Query the ecommerce_customers table with the following implementation logic:
   *
   * **Query Building**
   *
   * 1. Start with base SELECT on ecommerce_customers table
   * 2. Apply soft-delete filter: exclude deleted customers by default unless status filter explicitly requests 'deleted'
   * 3. Apply search filters:
   *    - display_name: ILIKE '%{value}%' for partial match
   *    - email: ILIKE '%{value}%' for partial match
   *    - created_at_gte: created_at >= {value}
   *    - created_at_lte: created_at <= {value}
   *    - status: 'active' WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, 'deleted' WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL
   * 4. Apply sorting based on request parameters (default: created_at DESC)
   * 5. Apply pagination: LIMIT {limit} OFFSET {offset}
   *
   * **Response Construction**
   *
   * 1. Query total count for pagination metadata
   * 2. Fetch customer records with selected fields
   * 3. Build IPageIEcommerceCustomer.ISummary response:
   *    - items: array of customer summaries (id, email, display_name, phone_number, created_at, deleted_at)
   *    - pagination: { limit, offset, total, has_more }
   *
   * **Validation Rules**
   *
   * - limit: 1-100 (default: 20)
   * - offset: >= 0 (default: 0)
   * - Sort fields must be from allowed list: display_name, email, created_at, updated_at
   * - Sort direction: 'asc' or 'desc' (default: 'desc')
   *
   * **Error Handling**
   *
   * - 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid authentication
   * - 403 Forbidden: Non-administrator access attempt
   * - 400 Bad Request: Invalid filter parameters or pagination values
   *
   * **Performance Considerations**
   *
   * - Use indexes on email, created_at, deleted_at columns
   * - Consider adding composite indexes for common filter combinations
   * - Implement query timeout to prevent long-running searches
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async index(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEcommerceCustomer.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIEcommerceCustomer.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchEcommerceCustomers({
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve a customer's complete profile information by their unique identifier.
   *
   * This operation returns the full customer entity including display name, phone number, and account timestamps. The requesting customer must match the requested customerId to ensure data privacy and isolation.
   *
   * **Authorization**
   *
   * Only the authenticated customer themselves can access their own profile. Customers cannot view other customers' profiles. The system validates that the authenticated customer ID matches the requested customerId before returning data.
   *
   * **Response Fields**
   *
   * The response includes the customer's display name (visible to other users), phone number (optional contact information), and account timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The email and password_hash are never exposed in the response for security reasons.
   *
   * **Error Handling**
   *
   * Returns 404 if the customer does not exist or has been deleted. Returns 403 if the authenticated customer does not match the requested customerId.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param customerId Unique identifier of the customer to retrieve (UUID format).
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor null
   * @x-autobe-specification Query the ecommerce_customers table by id UUID parameter.
   *
   * **Authorization Check**
   *
   * Validate that the authenticated customer's ID matches the {customerId} path parameter. Reject with 403 Forbidden if they do not match to enforce data isolation.
   *
   * **Database Query**
   *
   * SELECT id, display_name, phone_number, created_at, updated_at FROM ecommerce_customers WHERE id = {customerId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
   *
   * Do NOT select email or password_hash fields - these are never exposed in API responses.
   *
   * **Validation**
   *
   * - Validate {customerId} is a valid UUID format
   * - Check if customer exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL)
   * - Return 404 Not Found if customer does not exist or is deleted
   *
   * **Response Construction**
   *
   * Return IEcommerceCustomer with fields: id, display_name, phone_number, created_at, updated_at. Exclude email and password_hash for security.
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get(":customerId")
  public async at(
    @TypedParam("customerId")
    customerId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
  ): Promise<IEcommerceCustomer> {
    try {
      return await getEcommerceCustomersCustomerId({
        customerId,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

   * This endpoint provides a unified interface for viewing historical snapshots that preserve the state of entities at specific points in time. Snapshots are created automatically when entities are modified and serve as an immutable audit trail for dispute resolution and compliance verification.
   *

   * - Review snapshots: Record rating and content changes when reviews are edited
   * - Cancellation request snapshots: Track status transitions and responses throughout the cancellation workflow
   * - Refund request snapshots: Document refund request lifecycle including seller responses
   * - Seller profile snapshots: Preserve shop name, description, and logo changes over time
   *
   * **Access Control**
   *
   * - Sellers can view snapshots only for their own entities (products, variants, profile)
   * - Administrators can view all snapshots across all entity types
   * - Customer actors cannot access snapshot endpoints
   *
   * **Snapshot Immutability**
   *
   * All snapshots are immutable once created. They cannot be modified or deleted under any circumstances, even when the original entity is deleted. This ensures historical records are preserved for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria for filtering snapshots including entity type, date ranges, entity references, and pagination parameters.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null

   *
   * 1. **Validate Authorization**: Verify actor is seller or admin. Reject customer actors with 403 Forbidden.
   *
   * 2. **Apply Entity Type Filter**: Based on snapshotType in request:
   *    - 'product': Query ecommerce_product_snapshots with join to products for seller ownership validation
   *    - 'orderItem': Query ecommerce_order_item_snapshots with join to order_items for access validation
   *    - 'review': Query ecommerce_review_snapshots with join to reviews for access validation
   *    - 'cancellationRequest': Query ecommerce_cancellation_request_snapshots
   *    - 'refundRequest': Query ecommerce_refund_request_snapshots
   *    - 'seller': Query ecommerce_seller_snapshots
   *    - If not specified, query all snapshot types with UNION or separate queries
   *
   * 3. **Apply Ownership Filtering**:
   *    - For sellers: Filter snapshots where the related entity belongs to the seller (product.owner_id, seller_profile.seller_id, etc.)
   *    - For admins: No ownership filtering, return all matching snapshots
   *
   * 4. **Apply Search Filters**:
   *    - Date range: Filter by created_at between fromDate and toDate
   *    - Entity reference: Filter by specific entity ID (productId, orderItemId, etc.)

   * - Invalid snapshot type: Return 400 Bad Request

   * - Implement query result limiting to prevent excessive data retrieval

    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**

   *
   * Snapshots are immutable audit trails that preserve the historical state of entities at specific points in time. Each snapshot captures the complete state of an entity (product, order item, review, cancellation request, refund request, seller profile, or category) before a modification occurred.
   *
   * **Access Control**
   * - Entity owners can view snapshots of their own entities
   * - Administrators can view any snapshot on the platform
   * - Unauthorized access attempts return a 403 error without revealing whether the snapshot exists
   *

   * The response includes a type indicator to distinguish between:
   * - Product snapshots (preserving product name, description, category, price)
   * - Order item snapshots (preserving product and seller state at purchase)
   * - Review snapshots (preserving rating and content before edits)
   * - Cancellation request snapshots (preserving status transitions)
   * - Refund request snapshots (preserving refund request state)
   * - Seller profile snapshots (preserving shop name, description, logo)
   * - Category snapshots (preserving category hierarchy and details)
   *
   * **Immutability**
   * Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted. They are preserved indefinitely for audit and dispute resolution purposes.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param snapshotId Unique identifier of the snapshot record (UUID format).

   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor seller
   * @x-autobe-specification Query the appropriate snapshot table based on the snapshotId. Since snapshot IDs are unique across all snapshot types, implement a polymorphic query that checks each snapshot table (ecommerce_product_snapshots, ecommerce_order_item_snapshots, ecommerce_review_snapshots, ecommerce_cancellation_request_snapshots, ecommerce_refund_request_snapshots, ecommerce_seller_snapshots, ecommerce_category_snapshots) until a match is found.
   *
   * **Authorization**
   * 1. Extract the authenticated user from the request context
   * 2. Determine the snapshot type and associated entity
   * 3. Verify access:
   *    - If user is an administrator, allow access
   *    - If user owns the associated entity, allow access
   *    - Otherwise, deny with 403 Forbidden
   * 4. Do not reveal whether the snapshot exists if access is denied
   *
   * **Data Retrieval**
   * 1. Query snapshot tables sequentially or use a UNION query to find the snapshot by ID
   * 2. Return the complete snapshot record with:
   *    - Snapshot ID
   *    - Snapshot type indicator
   *    - All snapshot-specific fields (denormalized data)
   *    - Created timestamp
   *    - Reference to the parent entity
   *
   * **Error Handling**
   * - 404 Not Found: Snapshot does not exist
   * - 403 Forbidden: User lacks permission to view this snapshot
   * - 401 Unauthorized: User is not authenticated

  @TypedRoute.Get(":snapshotId")
  public async at(

    seller: SellerPayload,

    snapshotId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">,

    try {
      return await getEcommerceSellerSnapshotsSnapshotId({
        seller,
        snapshotId,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

import { TypedBody, TypedParam, TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";
import { Controller } from "@nestjs/common";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";

import { IEcommerceProduct } from "../../../api/structures/IEcommerceProduct";

import { getEcommerceProductsProductId } from "../../../providers/getEcommerceProductsProductId";
import { patchEcommerceProducts } from "../../../providers/patchEcommerceProducts";

@Controller("/ecommerce/products")
export class EcommerceProductsController {
  /**
   * Search and list products with pagination, filtering, and sorting capabilities.
   *
   * This endpoint retrieves a paginated list of products from the ecommerce_products table. Customers can browse products by name, category, price range, and other criteria. Sellers can filter by their own products. The response includes product summaries optimized for list displays with essential information like name, base price, category, and variant availability status.
   *
   * **Search Capabilities**
   * - Text search on product name using trigram matching
   * - Category filtering by category ID (includes subcategories option)
   * - Price range filtering (minimum and maximum base price)
   * - Seller filtering (for seller dashboard views)
   * - Pagination with cursor-based navigation
   * - Sorting by created_at, updated_at, name, or base_price
   *
   * **Business Rules**
   * - Soft-deleted products are excluded from results unless explicitly requested
   * - Products without variants are marked as unavailable in summaries
   * - Category filtering can include or exclude subcategory products
   * - Stock availability is calculated from inventory records on-demand
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria for product listing including text filters, category filters, price ranges, pagination parameters, and sorting options.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor null
   * @x-autobe-specification Implement product search with the following logic:
   *
   * 1. **Query Construction**
   *    - Query ecommerce_products table with filters from request body
   *    - Join with ecommerce_categories for category name in summaries
   *    - Join with ecommerce_sellers for seller name in summaries (if requested)
   *    - LEFT JOIN with ecommerce_product_variants to check variant availability
   *    - Filter out soft-deleted products (deleted_at IS NULL) by default
   *
   * 2. **Filter Application**
   *    - Name search: Use PostgreSQL trigram matching (name ILIKE %keyword% or gin_trgm_ops index)
   *    - Category filter: Match category_id exactly, optionally include subcategories via recursive CTE
   *    - Price range: Apply >= min_price AND <= max_price on base_price
   *    - Seller filter: Match seller_id for seller-specific views
   *    - Availability filter: Check if product has at least one non-deleted variant with stock > 0
   *
   * 3. **Stock Availability Calculation**
   *    - For each product, calculate total stock by summing all ecommerce_inventory_records for its variants
   *    - Mark product as 'available' if any variant has stock > 0
   *    - Mark product as 'out_of_stock' if all variants have stock = 0
   *    - Mark product as 'unavailable' if no variants exist
   *
   * 4. **Pagination**
   *    - Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at or id as cursor
   *    - Support limit (default 20, max 100) and cursor parameters
   *    - Return has_more flag indicating if additional pages exist
   *
   * 5. **Sorting**
   *    - Support sort_by: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'name', 'base_price'
   *    - Support sort_order: 'asc' or 'desc' (default 'desc' for created_at)
   *    - Apply sorting before pagination
   *
   * 6. **Error Handling**
   *    - Return 400 if invalid filter values (e.g., negative price)
   *    - Return 400 if invalid sort_by or sort_order values
   *    - Return 400 if cursor is malformed
   *
   * 7. **Performance Optimization**
   *    - Use existing indexes: name (gin_trgm_ops), category_id, seller_id, created_at
   *    - Add composite index on (category_id, deleted_at) for category filtering
   *    - Consider materialized view for stock calculations if performance issues arise
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async index(
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEcommerceProduct.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIEcommerceProduct.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchEcommerceProducts({
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Retrieve detailed information for a specific product including its seller, category, images, and variants.
   *
   * This endpoint returns the complete product entity with all associated data. The product must be active (not soft-deleted) to be accessible. Customers can browse products, sellers can view their own products, and administrators can view any product on the platform.
   *

import { TypedRoute } from "@nestia/core";

import { IEcommerceCategoryTree } from "../../../api/structures/IEcommerceCategoryTree";

@Controller("/ecommerce/tree")
export class EcommerceController {
  /**
   * Retrieve the complete category hierarchy tree structure for product browsing.
   *
   * This operation returns all active categories organized in a two-level hierarchy, showing root categories with their associated subcategories. Customers use this endpoint to browse the product catalog structure and navigate to specific category sections.
   *
   * **Response Structure**
   *
   * The response contains root-level categories, each including an array of their direct subcategories. Categories are filtered to exclude soft-deleted entries (deleted_at is null). Each category includes its identifier, name, description, and subcategory list.
   *
   * **Access Control**
   *
   * This endpoint is publicly accessible to all users including guests. No authentication is required as category browsing is a fundamental product discovery feature.
   *
   * **Error Handling**
   *
   * Returns 404 if no categories exist in the system. Returns 500 for database query failures.
   *
   * @param connection
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor null
   * @x-autobe-specification Query ecommerce_categories table for all active (deleted_at IS NULL) categories. Fetch root categories (parent_id IS NULL) with their subcategories using a single query with LEFT JOIN or two separate queries optimized for the two-level hierarchy.
   *
   * **Implementation Steps**
   *
   * 1. Query root categories where parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL, ordered by name ascending
   * 2. For each root category, fetch its subcategories where parent_id equals root id AND deleted_at IS NULL, ordered by name ascending
   * 3. Alternatively, use a single query fetching all active categories and group by parent_id in application code
   * 4. Build hierarchical response structure with root categories containing subcategory arrays
   * 5. Return empty array if no categories exist (not 404 - empty catalog is valid)
   *
   * **Database Queries**
   *
   * Option A (Two queries):
   * - SELECT id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at FROM ecommerce_categories WHERE parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY name
   * - SELECT id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at FROM ecommerce_categories WHERE parent_id IN (:rootIds) AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY name
   *
   * Option B (Single query with grouping):
   * - SELECT id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at FROM ecommerce_categories WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY COALESCE(parent_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'), name
   *
   * **Business Rules**
   *
   * - Only return categories where deleted_at IS NULL (soft delete filter)
   * - Root categories have parent_id = NULL
   * - Subcategories have exactly one parent (parent_id NOT NULL)
   * - Subcategories array should be empty for root categories with no children
   * - Category names are unique within the same parent level (enforced by @@unique constraint)
   *
   * **Edge Cases**
   *
   * - Empty category catalog: Return empty array []
   * - Root category with no subcategories: Include root with empty subcategories array
   * - All categories deleted: Return empty array []
   * - Large category tree: Consider pagination if catalog exceeds reasonable size (not required for typical use)
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Get()
  public async tree(): Promise<IEcommerceCategoryTree> {
    try {
      return await getEcommerceTree();
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}

@Controller("/ecommerce/customer/search")
export class EcommerceCustomerSearchController {
  /**
   * Search and browse products across the platform with filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities.
   *
   * This endpoint allows customers to discover products by applying various search criteria including name search, category filtering, price range filtering, and stock availability filtering. Results can be sorted by multiple criteria and returned in paginated format for efficient browsing.
   *
   * **Search Features**
   * - Full-text search on product names using trigram matching
   * - Category filtering including subcategories
   * - Price range filtering with minimum and maximum bounds
   * - Stock availability filtering (in stock, out of stock, or all)
   * - Sorting by newest, price ascending, or price descending
   * - Cursor-based pagination for large result sets
   *
   * **Business Rules**
   * - Only products from approved and non-suspended sellers are visible
   * - Soft-deleted products are excluded from search results
   * - Uncategorized products remain visible in search after category deletion
   * - Out of stock products are included but marked appropriately
   *
   * **Security**
   * - All customers have equal access to product browsing regardless of purchase history
   * - Seller approval status is checked before including products in results
   *
   * @param connection
   * @param body Search criteria including name keyword, category filters, price range, stock availability filter, sorting preference, and pagination parameters.
   * @x-autobe-authorization-type null
   * @x-autobe-authorization-actor customer
   * @x-autobe-specification Query ecommerce_products table with complex filtering and pagination.
   *
   * **Implementation Steps**
   *
   * 1. **Base Query**: Start with products table joined with sellers and categories
   *    - Filter: products.deleted_at IS NULL
   *    - Filter: sellers.approval_status = 'approved'
   *    - Filter: sellers.is_suspended = FALSE
   *    - Filter: sellers.deleted_at IS NULL
   *
   * 2. **Search Filters** (apply conditionally based on request):
   *    - Name search: Use PostgreSQL trigram matching (name ILIKE '%keyword%' or gin_trgm_ops index)
   *    - Category filter: Join with categories, filter by category_id OR parent_id for subcategory inclusion
   *    - Price range: Filter base_price BETWEEN min_price AND max_price
   *    - Stock availability: Join with product_variants and sum inventory_records, filter by stock > 0 or stock = 0
   *
   * 3. **Sorting**:
   *    - 'newest': ORDER BY products.created_at DESC
   *    - 'price_asc': ORDER BY products.base_price ASC
   *    - 'price_desc': ORDER BY products.base_price DESC
   *
   * 4. **Pagination**:
   *    - Use cursor-based pagination with created_at and id as cursor fields
   *    - Accept limit (default 20, max 100) and cursor parameters
   *    - Return next cursor for subsequent page requests
   *
   * 5. **Response Assembly**:
   *    - Join with sellers for shop_name
   *    - Join with categories for category_name
   *    - Calculate average rating from ecommerce_reviews (LEFT JOIN, AVG(rating))
   *    - Get main image from ecommerce_product_images (ORDER BY display_order ASC LIMIT 1)
   *    - Calculate current stock from sum of inventory_records for all variants
   *
   * 6. **Edge Cases**:
   *    - No search criteria provided: Return all visible products
   *    - No matching products: Return empty page with zero count
   *    - Invalid cursor: Return error or start from beginning
   *    - Price range with only min or only max: Apply partial filter
   *
   * 7. **Performance**:
   *    - Use indexes: name (gin_trgm_ops), category_id, seller_id, created_at
   *    - Consider materialized views for average rating if performance issues
   *    - Cache category hierarchy for subcategory filtering
   * @nestia Generated by Nestia - https://github.com/samchon/nestia
   */
  @TypedRoute.Patch()
  public async index(
    @CustomerAuth()
    customer: CustomerPayload,
    @TypedBody()
    body: IEcommerceProduct.IRequest,
  ): Promise<IPageIEcommerceProduct.ISummary> {
    try {
      return await patchEcommerceCustomerSearch({
        customer,
        body,
      });
    } catch (error) {
      console.log(error);
      throw error;
    }
  }
}
